lede: Tom built a big man's team, and it finished on the podium: fifth seed, 12–7, third place. It won field-goal percentage in 20 of 22 matchups, and that was the foundation. The odd part is the money. $42 of the $200 went on Trae Young, and he never played a minute in a Brighton lineup — he was on the Foxes before opening night, in the deal that brought back Josh Hart, who lasted ten days. 55% of the team's category value came from players it did not draft, and Nikola Jokic arrived on day 72.
profile:
Read the table top to bottom and the build is obvious. First in the league in FG% at .503, second in rebounds, third in blocks. Last in threes — 879 against a league average of 1,173 — and 13th in turnovers. A roster of centres pays for it in threes and giveaways, and that is a coherent trade: five categories won at 64% or better.

The threes were a punt (4–17–1). Free throws and steals at 36% were not. Those are the two categories where the shape leaked more than it had to.
ledger: 104 of 198 categories, playoffs included. Six regular-season weeks came down to a single category, and Brighton won five of them — the margin that turns a 4.5-a-week team into a 12–7 record. The soft patch was weeks 15 to 17: 2–6–1, 3–5–1, 3–5–1. The playoffs went the other way. A 7–2 win over The Infirmary, a 4–4–1 draw with Fantastic 5 that sent Fantastic 5 through, and a 7–2 win over Optimize the MVPs for third.
draft: Graded in categories a week, the draft was one star and one steal. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at $79 added 0.86 a week, the most on the roster and a little more than a $79 pick usually adds. Matas Buzelis at $8 was the best pick for the price: 0.45 a week, +0.19 over par, kept all season. Onyeka Okongwu at $4 was the one pick the board liked and the result backed: "good call, and it paid off". The costliest was Trae Young: $42 and nothing in this lineup, −0.53 against what a $42 pick usually adds. (The data only recovers Hart's side of that deal, so Young reads as dropped.) Kon Knueppel at $1 was also gone before the first lineup. He went on to a big season elsewhere, but his threes would have landed on a team that won threes in 18% of its matchups.
production: Over half the value came from outside the draft, and the best of it was found in the first fortnight. Amen Thompson (+0.56 a week) and Ryan Rollins (+0.49) were the second- and third-most valuable players on the team, both held all 19 weeks. Rollins was a day-4 claim for Nikola Jovic, and it is the best lasting wire move of the season: +0.40 a week for 19 weeks. Jokic is the complicated one. +0.39 a week across the nine weeks he was held, but he started only five of them. In the playoffs he added 1.83 over three weeks, more than anyone else on the roster.
trades: Seven trades recovered of the nine ESPN counts. Three have only one side in the data and are not graded. The four that can be graded all came out below zero in the regular season, for different reasons. Day 5, Queta and Schroder for Okongwu: poor call, and it cost you (−0.25 expected, −0.05 a week over 11 weeks). Day 49, Kyshawn George for Franz Wagner: good call, bad break. At the time Wagner was worth +0.15 a week more, but he started two of his next ten weeks, and it delivered −0.32. Day 72, Avdija and Okongwu for Jokic, is the one to argue about: unlucky in the regular season (−0.25 a week over nine weeks, with Jokic starting five), then a lucky break in the playoffs (+0.14). Day 76, Clingan for Jalen Duren, was a wash at the time and −0.25 in the result.
wire: 56 claims won from 210 attempts, $98 of FAAB, top bid $21. The average move added +0.08 categories a week against the player it replaced, seventh of 14. Every team's wire work is positive on this measure, so the middle is the honest read. The best of it was early and lasting: Ryan Rollins on day 4 (+0.40 a week for 19 weeks) and Jaime Jaquez Jr. on day 13 ("good call, and it paid off", +0.33 for 17). The costliest lasting move was day 70, Ivica Zubac for Jarrett Allen: a good call on paper, −0.23 a week over seven weeks.
bench: Fifteen wasted player-days, sixth in the league, and one bad day accounts for a lot of it. Day 104: OG Anunoby 42, Ryan Rollins 39, Jalen Duren 36 and Ivica Zubac 35, all on the bench at once — 152 production sitting down in week 15, a matchup lost 2–6–1. Whether there was room to start them depends on who held the slots that day. Either way, it was the worst day of the season.
last: The third-place game, and Brighton treated it like a final. 70 starting slots set against 68, 44 of them producing a game against 39, and a 7–2 win. Rebounds 271 to 199, blocks 30 to 11 — the season's shape, intact in its last week.
closing:
A good season, honestly earned. The identity was clear from the draft — bigs, field-goal percentage, the glass — and it held for twenty-two weeks and a podium finish.

Two things to take into next year. First, premium money went on players the team never kept: $42 on a guard gone before opening night, the worst pick for the price on this roster. Second, the trades. Every one that can be graded came out below zero in the regular season. Two were decent calls that broke badly (Wagner, Jokic), and the day-5 deal was a poor call from the start.

And decide on the leaks. Threes were a real punt. Free throws and steals at 36% were not, and a single guard held all year would have turned some of those into wins.
